summary: Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya works in Indology and philosophy. He was a Professor at Vidyasagar College (attested 1970–1975) and served in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta, where he was attested as Lecturer in 1982 and faculty in 1994.

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. His career includes posts at the University of Leipzig, Heidelberg University, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Muhamad Saputra is a doctoral student at the Australian National University (attested 2026), studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.

Muhamed Riyaz Chenganakkattil is an Indology and history scholar who earned MAs from Darul Huda Islamic University and Jamia Millia Islamia, and a PhD from IIT Delhi (2016–2024). In 2024, he held fellowships at IIT Delhi and Ghent University.

Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He has served as Deputy Director at the Taxila Museum, Director of the Department of Archaeology and Museums in Andhra Pradesh, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).

Muhammad Nasim Khan is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned an M.Phil from the University of Peshawar, later serving there as Assistant Professor, alongside visiting appointments at the University of Hamburg and the Royal Asiatic Society.

Muhammad Shahidullah (1885–1969) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Calcutta, Presidency, and Paris under Sylvain Lévi, he held long-term posts at the University of Dhaka (~1921–1954), the University of Rajshahi, the Bangla Academy, and Islamic Foundation Bangladesh.

Muhammed Niyas Ashraf is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin (2015–2024) and held a postdoctoral fellowship at Ghent University (2025–2026).

Mukesh Mehta specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at Banaras Hindu University (2019–2022) and was a Research Associate at the International School for Jain Studies in 2023.

Mukund Lalji Wadekar is an Indologist who served as Officiating Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 2002–2008), Officiating Director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 2008), and General Editor of the Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 2008).

Mukund Ram Shastri (d. 1921) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Head Pandit at the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir, attested in 1911 and from 1916 to 1918.

Mukunda Raj Aryal is a history and Indology scholar. He earned an MBA from Apex College and an M.Phil. from Tribhuvan University, and held posts as Professor at Tribhuvan University (attested 2003) and Head at Apex College (2017).

Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Hanazono University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), abbot of Shofuku-ji (~1949–1988), and head of the Institute for Zen Studies.

Mun-keat Choong is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and completed an MA and PhD at the University of Queensland under Roderick S. Bucknell, later serving as Lecturer in Studies in Religion at the University of New England (2003–2025).

Munenobu Sakurai (b. 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. After completing doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1985–1990), he served as assistant professor at Iwate University and professor at Tohoku University (attested 2005, 2026).

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indologist. After studies at Kyoto University and a PhD from Harvard (~1974–1982), he was an associate professor at Tokyo Institute of Technology before serving as associate professor and professor at Kyoto University (~1987–2010).

Muneyoshi Yanagi (1889–1961) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1910–1913) and was a student of Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki (~1910–1920).

Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar in religious studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Brigitte Marschall (attested 2010).

Munis D. Faruqui (b. 1967) is an Indology and history scholar. He has served as Associate Professor at the University of California, Berkeley (2005) and held positions at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (~2014).

Munish Chandra Joshi (1935–2007) worked in archaeology and Indology. He served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (~1987–1989) and Member Secretary at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (~1995–2000).
